title: POC Weekly Sync — Model Selection & Pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results across candidate models, decide on model/version pinning strategy, and plan canary & rollback behavior. Customer prefers hosted for speed but wants fallback to smaller models and clear rollback process. SE to deliver pin config and benchmark spreadsheet; next canary scheduled after tests in EU region.
next_steps: Maya to share detailed benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs by 2026-01-15
Carlos to draft recommended pinning config (primary + fallback + canary windows) by 2026-01-16
Jonas to provide production traffic sample for canary sizing by 2026-01-14
Schedule 2-hour canary run in EU region week of 2026-01-19
action_items: Maya Chen - share benchmark CSV + shortnotes (due 2026-01-15)
Carlos Rivera - propose pinning JSON + rollback playbook (due 2026-01-16)
Jonas Meyer - export 24h production traffic sample and send link (due 2026-01-14)
Priya Singh - confirm success criteria for canary (latency p95 < 350ms, quality delta < 1.5% on eval set) (due 2026-01-14)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-12 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45 min | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Head of ML - Nimbus), Jonas Meyer (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Product)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have the usual agenda — quick recap of last week's benchmarks, dig into model selection and pinning, and decide next steps. anyone on the call new?
[00:10] Anika (Nimbus): hey, this is Anika, still with us. Jonas and Priya are here too.
[00:14] Jonas (Nimbus): yep hi all.
[00:16] Maya: great. Carlos, want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood SE): sure, i've got the trimmed benchmark that we ran on your sample workload, 1000 requests sampled from the ecommerce search assistant. we tested three family variants: rdx-alpha-1 (our curated variant), meta-llama-2-13b (quantized to 4-bit), and llama-3-7b-int8. i summarized p50/p95 latency, tokens per response, and cost per 1k responses.
[01:05] Carlos: quick headline — on hosted infra in us-west the rdx-alpha-1 v1.2 gave best quality on our eval set (fewer hallucinations, higher rerank NDCG) but p95 was ~420ms versus 320ms for the 7b int8. cost per 1k tokens was about 1.8x higher for the 13b quantized.
[01:35] Priya (Nimbus): the quality delta matters — on our product, a hallucinated price or availability is a non-starter. so i'm inclined to favor the rdx variant if latency is still acceptable. what's our fallback plan if alpha-1 hits a bad tail latency?
[01:55] Carlos: that's where pinning + fallback comes in. propose primary pin to rdx-alpha-1@v1.2 for the pilot, with a fallback to llama-3-7b-int8@v3.0 when latency exceeds threshold or queue depth grows. canary traffic to be 5-10% for 2 hours, then ramp. we can also set an automatic fallback policy based on p95 > 500ms for three consecutive minutes.
[02:30] Anika: can we do region-specific pins? we have EU customers and data residency concerns there.
[02:38] Maya: yes, Redwood supports route-level pinning; you can pin different versions by region. for EU we'll recommend the same primary but we can run the canary on a dedicated zone to test infra differences.
[02:50] Jonas: on the dedicated vs hosted question — we prefer hosted for the POC for speed, but later may move to dedicated. any differences in pin behavior between hosted and dedicated?
[03:05] Carlos: functionally consistent. the main differences are kernel selections and performance variance across hardware. dedicated gives you more predictable p95 but requires reserved capacity planning. for the POC hosted is fine.
[03:20] Priya: what about KV cache and prefix caching? can that reduce cost/latency if we stick with the larger model?
[03:28] Carlos: yes we saw 20-30% token reduction with prefix caching on repeated prompts in your sample. caching helps more with mid-sized sessions; for first-turn search queries it's limited. still worth enabling for the pilot.
[03:45] Maya: let's talk pin versions explicitly. Carlos, what's your recommended pin set?
[03:48] Carlos: recommend: primary rdx-alpha-1@1.2 (quality), fallback llama-3-7b-int8@3.0 (cost/latency), emergency fallback meta-llama-2-13b-q4@2.1 only if both others fail. Canary config: 7% traffic for 2 hours, health checks on latency/p99 errors and our eval prompt pass rate. Rollback: immediate switch to fallback and notify on-call, then a human review.
[04:20] Anika: about the eval prompt pass rate — can we embed our product-specific prompts for automated monitoring?
[04:26] Carlos: absolutely — you can provide a set of 200 golden prompts and we run continuous quality checks. that'll be part of the monitoring dashboard.
[04:35] Priya: do we have examples of false positives where fallback triggered too often due to transient infra blips?
[04:40] Maya: yes we had one POC where the p95 threshold triggered during a noisy neighbor event; we improved policy by adding a two-minute smoothing window and checking request queue depth. we can share that playbook.
[04:55] Jonas: latency numbers you gave were us-west — what's the EU p95?
[05:02] Carlos: EU p95 for rdx-alpha-1 was ~480ms on the host we tested; 7b-int8 was ~360ms. that's why region-specific canary is important.
[05:15] Anika: so if EU is 480ms p95 that's high for user experience. can we consider pinning EU to the 7b-int8 as primary and US to alpha?
[05:24] Carlos: yes, we can do that. you can have route-based pins by region or by route name. recommended approach: keep the high-quality model for core routes where hallucination risk is high, use 7b-int8 for latency-sensitive read-only routes.
[05:40] Priya: what about cost modelling? how accurate are your cost numbers?
[05:45] Carlos: the cost numbers are estimates based on tokens and our published unit pricing; for POC we'll give a detailed spreadsheet with per-model token breakdowns and projected monthly cost for your expected qps.
[05:58] Maya: i'll attach that spreadsheet after the call.
[06:02] Anika: security / compliance check — we need to confirm logs and audit trails, and KMS usage for any private deployment.
[06:09] Maya: we have SOC2 docs and KMS options. for hosted we'll store minimal logs by default but can enable full audit retention; keys can be customer-managed in Private deployments. i'll include the SOC2 + compliance pack.
[06:22] Jonas: on rollbacks — do we get request-level traceback to identify which inputs triggered regressions?
[06:28] Carlos: yes, request-level traces and sample payload capture are available, subject to PII redaction settings. we also provide token-level cost breakdown per request.
[06:36] Priya: curious about canary metrics — what's the failure criteria? p95 and our eval pass rate? also error rate?
[06:42] Carlos: primary failure triggers: p95 > 1.3x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes, error rate spike > 0.5% absolute, or eval pass rate drop > 1.5% on the golden set. Those are configurable.
[06:58] Anika: ok sounds reasonable. what about rollout tooling — can we do A/B testing for quality metrics, not just traffic splits?
[07:05] Maya: yes, Redwood Console has route-aware split and can record quality metrics from your evaluations to compare.
[07:12] Jonas: i want to confirm the actual pin config file format — is it a JSON we can version control?
[07:17] Carlos: exact — it's a simple JSON manifest with routes, primary, fallbacks, canary settings, and health checks. we'll send an example.
[07:25] Priya: any gotchas we should be aware of? like model drift after a few days?
[07:29] Carlos: model drift is more about prompt distribution changing; for POC duration probably small, but we recommend periodic evals and daily sampling to catch regressions. also if you enable quantized variants, watch for subtle output differences on edge cases.
[07:45] Maya: okay let's make the decision items explicit — which model to pin as primary for the pilot?
[07:50] Anika: i'd like primary = rdx-alpha-1@1.2 for the core commerce intent routes; but for EU, and for latency-sensitive search-suggestions route, use llama-3-7b-int8@3.0 as primary. fallback policy as Carlos suggested.
[08:05] Jonas: agree. we'll provide route list and traffic estimates by tomorrow.
[08:10] Priya: success criteria: stability for 24h at p95 < 350ms on search-suggestions, quality delta < 1.5% on checkout-critical prompts.
[08:20] Maya: noted. next steps recap: share spreadsheet, send pin JSON example, schedule canary in EU.
[08:25] Carlos: i'll assemble the pin manifest and rollback playbook.
[08:30] Anika: thanks all, real quick — can you also share the playbook for emergency rollback that includes comms templates?
[08:36] Maya: yes, we'll include comms templates and a runbook.
[08:40] Priya: anything else?
[08:42] Jonas: no, that's it. thanks.
[08:45] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll circle next week same time unless we run the canary earlier. bye.

End of transcript. Note: occasional transcription errors in product names (we sometimes see rdx-alpha transcribed as red x alpha) and timestamps approximate.
